chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd bin Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad bin Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Ahmad bin al-Nadr, from Amr bin Shamar, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said: Jibra'il (peace be upon him) informed me that the wind of Paradise is found from the journey of a thousand years. It will not be found by a disobedient son, nor one who cuts kinship relations, nor an old man who fornicates, nor one whose robe drags in haughtiness, nor one who causes seduction, nor one who offers favor (to humiliate), nor a Ja'dhari. He said: I said: And what is a Ja'dhari? He said: The one who is not satisfied with this world.

key_terms.جَارُ إِزَارِهِ خِيَاءٌ: One whose robe drags in haughtiness/pride
key_terms.جَعْظَرِيٌّ: A term for one who is insatiable or greedy
key_terms.مُنَّانٌ: One who offers favor to humiliate

ai.seo_question: What are the specific sins that cause one to miss the wind of Paradise?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* highlights the spiritual olfactory perception of Paradise, linking the scent of Jannah to specific moral failings such as severing kinship ties (qat' al-rahim) and arrogance (kibr). It concludes by defining the 'Ja'dhari' as one consumed by insatiable greed for the world, a concept deeply rooted in Shia ethical teachings on purifying the soul from dunya-obsession.
